highlights.title: Aqara goes all in on smart lighting
highlights.summary: After showing off several smart home firsts at CES, Aqara has returned to IFA with a major lineup of smart lighting compatible with both Zigbee and Thread. One of these new devices is the Floor Lamp T1, which trades the look of a typical lamp for an LED-equipped pole attached to a base.
body: A new floor lamp, outdoor smart lighting, and LED strip from Aqara support Zigbee and Thread.

The lamp stands 4.6 feet tall, offering RGBIC lighting and 18 individually addressable zones. Similar to the floor lamp from Govee, Aqara’s new device emits light in the area surrounding it, creating a splash of color on your wall.

Aqara is getting into smart lighting for the outside of your home as well. In addition to new permanent outdoor smart lights with individually addressable LEDs, Aqara is launching RGBIC string lights that can be customized with a range of colors for holidays, or set to warm and cool white lighting options for ambience.

The company is also updating its LED light strip, which comes with the same 16 million color range as its predecessor, but adds a new chip that supports multi-zone control with 18 independent zones per 3-meter section. Aqara is launching a second-gen downlight as well, with 4- and 6-inch sizes that offer either RGB-CCT (colors plus tunable white) or just RGB.

highlights.title: The sameness problem behind those unappetizing AI-generated menus
highlights.summary: While restaurant owners might look to generative AI as a shortcut to sprucing up their menu, customers can viscerally sense that something is wrong with the food.
body: When it first happens to you, you think you’re crazy. You wander into a cafe and look at a menu with a variety of bagel sandwiches, but each illustration looks eerily flawless, precisely symmetrical, and oddly smooth, eliciting a visceral sensation that something isn’t right. You might think you’re paranoid, but you’re not losing your mind. Generative AI menus have hit the restaurant business courtesy of models trained on a narrow, “pleasing” aesthetic that feels wrong even when you can’t articulate why.

Sometimes, these illustrations are egregiously fake, like a burrito with cheese so bubbly and melty that it looks more like avant garde art than lunch. More often, they’re so ordinary looking that you only notice something is wrong when you take a second to look more closely.

Lisle says that the way these models are built can help explain why illustrations seem to embrace such a specific aesthetic — one where every ice cream scoop is perfectly round, and where shrimp seem to have been genetically modified to eat their own tails, creating new “ Lovecraftian food horrors.”

highlights.title: Andrews: Brentford are playing with verve - let's see if we can break the ceiling
highlights.summary: Seconds before the curtain came down on the 2025/26 season, Brentford had a golden chance to do what they had never done before: qualify for Europe.
body: They were drawing 1-1 with Liverpool at Anfield and knew that one goal would be enough to finish seventh and secure Europa League football.

In the 10th minute of added time, Mikkel Damsgaard dropped the ball off to Vitaly Janelt on the left-hand side of the penalty area. The midfielder hit a cross first time that curled in the most inviting way to the centre of the box.
Kevin Schade was waiting for it, but Dango Ouattara got there first - and steered it off target.
Keith Andrews put his head in his hands and sank to his knees. His first season as a head coach had nearly ended in the most perfect way.

highlights.title: 8 Near-Perfect Anime To Watch if You Like 'Solo Leveling'
highlights.summary: In Solo Leveling, gifted Hunters fight vicious beasts to protect humanity, but the notoriously weak Sung Jin-woo finds himself trapped in a hopeless survival loop. Whereas the power levels of all Hunters are fixed, Jin-woo is chosen by the enigmatic "System" and is given the ability to accrue…
body: Some anime stories rely on exaggerated power fantasies to prop up a stand-out protagonist, but Solo Leveling takes it to another level. This trope can take many forms when used for sustained dramatic effect in genres like shonen or isekai. Shows like One-Punch Man come alive thanks to satirical deadpan humor while still delivering on the power fantasy. Others, like The Eminence in Shadow, embrace a ludicrous brand of self-aware absurdity. By contrast, Solo Leveling, which is based on a fantasy web novel by Chugong (later adapted into an immensely popular manhwa), uses addictive dungeon-crawler elements and RPG-style power progression to keep things dynamic and interesting.

Based on the Korean web novel and manhwa by Sanji Jiksong, Tomb Raider King might be the closest spiritual successor to Solo Leveling on this list. Mysterious tombs have appeared around the world, each containing powerful relics drawn from mythology and history. Ruthless corporations quickly turn their recovery into a lucrative industry, employing raiders like Seo Joo-Heon to brave the tombs on their behalf.

highlights.title: Lexar’s Muse is an ultra-slim portable SSD that’s less than 4mm thick
highlights.summary: Following the lead of companies like Xteink, Lexar is the latest to sacrifice a USB-C port in the pursuit of slimming down its hardware. When the Lexar Muse Ultra-Slim Portable SSD launches later this year in 512GB and 1TB capacities it will be one of the slimmest you can buy.
body: You can slim down your portable storage if you don’t mind dealing with a proprietary USB-C cable.

The downside is that without a standard USB-C port, you’ll need to rely on — and make sure not to lose — Lexar’s proprietary SnapLink cable that magnetically attaches to a pogo-pin connector on the side of the drive. The company doesn’t specify the strength of the magnets, but this approach also means there’s an increased risk of the cable being accidentally knocked off during a file transfer. And if you are using the Muse to record videos through your phone, you’ll need to slip it into an included magnetic sleeve in order to mount it to the back of your device, adding quite a bit of thickness in the process.

highlights.title: Nobody Is Saying Why OpenAI and Anthropic Had Outages Today
highlights.summary: ChatGPT, Claude, and Grok all suffered outages at nearly the exact same time for reasons that remain murky.
body: Frontier models from Anthropic, OpenAI, and xAI all experienced rare outages on Thursday morning, creating downtime for their corresponding AI chatbots. SpaceX, xAI’s parent company, said on Thursday afternoon that the issues with Grok resulted from “an outage at our Memphis compute center this morning.”

The issues initially appeared to be linked because they coincided—perhaps the result of a shared third-party service provider—but neither OpenAI nor Anthropic cited an external source in comments to WIRED on Thursday. SpaceX, xAI’s parent company, did not respond to WIRED’s request for comment. But the company said as part of its public comments on Thursday: “We’d also like to apologize to our impacted compute partners.” Anthropic and xAI announced a “compute partnership” with SpaceX in May.

OpenAI spokesperson Kathleen Chaykowski tells WIRED: “A routing error starting around 7:43 am PT on Thursday, September 3, made ChatGPT and Codex unavailable for some users across platforms. As of about 8:17 am PT on Thursday, a solution was successfully implemented and is continuing to be monitored.”

highlights.summary: Netflix’s animated musical Kpop Demon Hunters was an unexpected sensation, spending a full year in the streaming service’s global top 10 list. The film about a K-pop band whose music secretly empowers a mystical barrier protecting the world from demons racked up more than 500 million views…
body: A sequel is in the works, but it will likely be years until its release given how long animation takes to produce. Netflix is also working on launching a global concert tour. But a new treat for Kpop Demon Hunters fans is arriving in three weeks. Forgotten Island, an original DreamWorks Animation film from Puss in Boots: The Last Wish co-directors Joel Crawford and Januel Mercado, combines demons, music, and a sweet story about female friendship for a fantasy film that is likely to resonate with anyone obsessed with Huntrix and the Saja Boys.

Set in the Philippines in the 1990s, Forgotten Island follows best friends Jo (H.E.R.) and Raissa (Liza Soberano). When Raissa is admitted to Caltech, Jo insists they spend one last memorable night together. While they just plan on goofing off on the beach, they wind up finding a portal to Nakali, a mystical realm from the stories told by Jo’s grandmother.

highlights.title: ‘Oasis’ Director on Asking Uncomfortable Questions About Exclusion and Why Violence Is “Like a Virus”
highlights.summary: A viral video of a pupil threatening his classmates leads him and two fellow adolescent outcasts to seek refuge in a forest in German writer-director Jannis Lenz's feature debut, premiering at Venice.
body: “Oasis” feels like a bit of a theme at Venice this year, with at least two movies featuring that word in their titles. One is Will Lovelace and Dylan Southern’s Oasis: Don’t Look Back in Anger, a documentary about the reunion tour of the famous English rock band. But it is the other film that could leave audiences truly rocked.

In the film, world-premiering on Sept. 6 in the Horizons section of the 83rd edition of the Venice Film Festival, a viral video of a student threatening his classmates surfaces online, causing concern among school staff, parents and kids. The student shown in the video and two other outcasts end up seeking refuge in a nearby forest. Their play turns into ritual, with pain becoming an escape. But then old wounds surface and, as notes on the film highlight, the boundaries between them are redrawn.

Boundaries were fluid behind the scenes of the production. For example, Lenz directed Oasis based on a screenplay that he wrote with Alexander Dirninger, who also served as director of photography. Lenz also collaborated with Melisa Krasniqi in the editing process.

highlights.title: Helen Goh’s recipe for brown butter apple and blackberry bars | The sweet spot
highlights.summary: A bar for the bountiful season, with a rubbly oat crust, a soft fruit filling and a crisp topping. September is always a wistful time for me. Summer has all but slipped away, the days are noticeably shorter and the children are heading back to school.
body: These will keep for up to three days in an airtight container, and also freeze well, wrapped individually for convenience.

Grease and line a 20cm x 30cm baking tin with greaseproof paper, leaving enough overhang to help lift out the bars later. Put the butter in a medium saucepan on a medium heat and cook, swirling the pan occasionally, for about five minutes, until it smells nutty and the milk solids turn a deep golden brown. Take off the heat, stir in the anise seeds, if using, then leave to cool for five minutes.

Heat the oven to 200C (180C fan)/390F/gas 6. Meanwhile, mix the plain flour, rolled oats, oat flour, brown sugar and salt in a large bowl. Pour over the browned butter, including all the toasted milk solids, and mix until evenly moistened. The mixture should resemble damp sand and hold together when squeezed.

Reserve about 350g of the crumb mix for the topping, then tip the rest into the lined tin, pressing firmly into an even layer; use the base of a measuring cup or back of a spoon. This will help the bars hold together neatly when slicing. Bake for 18 minutes, until lightly golden around the edges.

highlights.summary: RugOne's Xsnap 7 Pro comes with both an IP68 and IP69K rating, meaning the rugged phone can survive intense water blasts and complete submersion for up to 30 minutes. But what really sets the Xsnap 7 Pro apart from everything else on the market is that one of its three rear cameras can be removed…
body: The Xsnap 7 Pro’s four cameras include a pop-out wearable action cam and a night vision camera that can see in the dark.
If you buy something from a Verge link, Vox Media may earn a commission. See our ethics statement.

The Xsnap 7 Pro’s detachable camera module isn’t quite as a capable as the DJI Osmo Nano or the Insta360 Go Ultra that both record at 4K. Its video capabilities max out at 2.7K at up to 30fps captured through a 133-degree ultrawide field-of-view lens. Video is processed by distortion correction algorithms to keep subjects looking natural, while software stabilization helps smooth out footage even when the camera is flipped 360 degrees, RugOne claims.

The action cam’s battery keeps it recording for up to 40 minutes, which can be extended to up to 800 minutes when repeatedly docked and charged using the phone’s own 9,300mAh battery. The camera’s 64GB of built-in storage can hold up to eight hours of 1080p footage, but videos can be transferred to the Xsnap 7 Pro’s 512GB of storage every time it’s docked. Waterproofing for the camera is slightly better than the phone, as it can be used to a depth of 5 meters instead of just 2.

highlights.title: Inside the neighbourhood club that made Arteta, Alonso and Iraola
highlights.summary: Between a row of white apartment buildings and an artificial pitch set into the green hills of Berio in San Sebastian that Antiguoko now call home, there is a strip of land where Mikel Arteta, Xabi Alonso and Andoni Iraola learned their craft.
body: "The centre circle was just over there," says Roberto Montiel, the club's long-serving coach and vice-president, as he takes a seat in what is now a public park. He rubs his thumb and forefinger together as he recalls the texture of the old playing surface.

"The pitch wasn't like the new one up there. It was smaller and made of small stones, like gravel. The balls weren't like the ones now either. When they got wet, they became heavy. You would slip and slide, and if you fell, you'd end up with a terrible scrape."
The games played here by this neighbourhood club's celebrated alumni, two of whom meet as managers when Arsenal face Chelsea on Sky Sports on Sunday, are the stuff of local legend.
"Even then you could see their vision for the game," adds Montiel.

Specifically, it's the version of Spider-Man depicted in a short-lived 1977 television series featuring the wall-crawling hero. But it also brings back memories of what might be the weirdest Spider-Man series ever.

highlights.title: Anna Foglietta on Working With Alba Rohrwacher on Venice Drama ‘A Common Story’ ‘You Have to Have the Guts to Show Yourself Exactly as You Are’ — Trailer (EXCLUSIVE)
highlights.summary: Actor-turned director Anna Foglietta is back in Venice in a different guise this year, after serving as the event’s official emcee in 2020. Foglietta — who is best-known to international audiences for her role in Italy’s smash hit “Perfect Strangers” — is on the Lido with her directorial debut, “A…
body: Foglietta spoke to Variety about working with Rohrwacher and shares her thoughts about Venice’s gender imbalance.

From my observation of the world. I spend a lot of time with the parents of my children’s friends. I’ve realized that, even observing myself as a parent, we’ve truly become too child-centric. Our obsession with everything a child does from the moment it is born is perhaps the fundamental alibi that allows us to effectively avoid taking care of ourselves [as adults].

There is a whole generation that does not really know itself and doesn’t have the will or the desire to do so. So together with screenwriter Matteo Ferri, with whom I wrote the story, I started to think about how to bring these elements together. I thought about a very simple couple. I’m very passionate about the part of humanity that never basks in the spotlight. They deploy energies and strategies to keep this world turning, but nobody cares. It always seems that great revolutions, even profound emotional and psychoanalytic ones, are always the prerogative of the bourgeoisie just because they have all the right cultural tools.

highlights.title: Experience: I didn’t know I was pregnant until I gave birth
highlights.summary: There’d been no morning sickness, cravings or tiredness. My mum didn’t believe I’d had a baby – even after seeing her on FaceTime. When I was 19, I went to college in Texas, where I met my ­boyfriend Preston. It was 2023 and I had big plans.
body: In May 2025, I took a trip to London, returning to campus in August after the summer holidays. I noticed I was slowly gaining weight; by January this year I’d gained 10lb. I put it down to my late-night snacking and lack of exercise.
But then on 20 February, after I had returned to my apartment following my morning class, I felt cramps in my lower stomach. At 1pm, I took some ibuprofen.

At 6.20pm, I felt a sudden urge to go to the toilet. After sitting there for a while with nothing happening, I stood up, assuming I was constipated. Then, I felt something strange happening between my legs. I looked down and saw something bulging out of me. I froze. I thought it was a tumour and that I was going to die.

But then I felt the urge to push – and suddenly there was a baby’s head between my thighs. I was terrified, but primal instinct took over. I waddled to my bedroom and grabbed a clean towel. I laid it down and dropped to my hands and knees. The adrenaline was pumping so hard that I don’t remember feeling pain. Three quick pushes later, I was able to grab my baby. Laying her on the floor in front of me, I rubbed her chest to help her cry. I did it all without thinking. Then I called 911.

body: Ready or Not 2: Here I Come, which is now available for streaming on Hulu, is the precise opposite of that.

This is a movie about a squadron of people who are forced to work outside their core competencies, because they do not have any. That doesn't mean they aren't dangerous, but it's often not in the way that they'd like to be. In the age of the Business Idiot, there's a sick thrill to watching the sons and daughters of privilege instantly crash and burn, and that thrill is most of what drives Ready or Not 2.
As it's a direct sequel, it's difficult to discuss Ready or Not 2 without disclosing parts of 2019's Ready or Not. Some spoilers follow.

In the original Ready or Not, Grace (Samara Weaving) discovers on her wedding night that her new husband's family owe their wealth and privilege to a demonic pact. As part of that pact, Grace is set loose on the family estate and hunted down as a human sacrifice. Grace survives. Her former in-laws don't.

highlights.title: Nvidia will officially bring DLSS 5 to older GPUs — but won’t give gamers full control
highlights.summary: Officially, Nvidia's controversial DLSS 5 AI rendering was supposed to launch this evening with only a single game, only on Nvidia's latest RTX 50 GPUs, and with developers in full control of their artistic vision.
body: Nvidia won’t confirm that previously announced DLSS 5 games will still ship with the tech.

But unofficially, modders have already ported a leaked version of DLSS 5 to run on just about anything while cranking sliders to the max. Now, Nvidia is changing its plans. DLSS 5 is still launching first on RTX 50 GPUs, but it’s officially coming to older RTX 40-series GPUs as well, Nvidia spokesperson Rajal Maharaj confirms to The Verge.

“Our current focus is on optimizing performance for the GeForce RTX 50 Series with model updates expected later this fall. Once RTX 50 Series performance is more fully tuned, we plan to work on expanding official support to the GeForce RTX 40 Series,” reads part of Nvidia’s statement.

What about earlier RTX 30 and RTX 20-series GPUs, which modders successfully targeted as well, assuming you count “not exactly playable framerate and plenty of crashes” as successful? “Right now the focus is of course on 50-series,” Maharaj tells me. “Once we feel like the 50-series is in a good place, we’re going to look at the 40-series.”

Ripe fruit would fall off trees and be eaten by dogs, earning avocados the unappetising name dog fruit, he says.

Bopaiah has been working in India's plantation industry for 26 years, he's currently group manager at Cottanad Plantations, which grows cocoa, rubber, coffee, spices and fruits, including avocado, in the hills of Wayanad in the southern Indian state of Kerala.
"We never planted avocado as our main crop. We introduced it as a shade tree for coffee plantations, and only later realised it could become a profitable business," he says.

highlights.title: ‘If you can’t understand what sex is, it’s irrelevant if you seem to be enjoying it’: how Queen at Sea upended the dementia drama
highlights.summary: Lance Hammer’s first film in 18 years is a heart-wrenching masterpiece about family, mental decline and sexual consent. He and supporting actor Juliette Binoche discuss how they brought unabashed realism to a condition rarely seen on screen.
body: The first time we see Martin and Leslie, the elderly couple at the centre of Lance Hammer’s wrenching new film, Queen at Sea, they are walking together up a set of stone steps: one of their regular outings, we assume, in days filled with pottering and quiet companionship. They have their backs to us, and we can’t see their destination beyond a bleached sky that fills the top half of the screen. Symbolically, it may be deemed a bit on the nose: two people near the end of their lives, moving gently towards the white light of oblivion. There’s a whiff of sentimentality about it.

But any doubts about this story’s willingness to confront difficult truths are blasted away by the next scene. Leslie’s daughter, Amanda, played by Juliette Binoche, pays a visit to the couple’s house in drizzly, middle-class north London, her teenage daughter in tow. Unable to find her mother and stepfather, she arrives at the bedroom door. Opening it, she finds Martin (Tom Courtenay) on top of Leslie (Anna Calder-Marshall), who lies impassively beneath him, the mask of dementia obvious on her face.
